its OWN row, not an alias of Olive Oil (owner ruling): the two are different foods — one is the cold-pressed finishing oil a recipe names on purpose, the other the refined cooking oil. A line that says plain "olive oil" still lands on Olive Oil. Macros are the same 100 % fat as any olive oil, so they are borrowed from the refined FDC record with that stated; the density is extra virgin's own FDC record.

the plain-peas row the vocabulary was missing — Frozen Peas is a product form, and a line that says "garden peas" should not have to claim it. Split rather than aliased (owner ruling); Frozen Peas is unchanged.

joins the Canned * family so a 400 g can of lentils has an honest target. The dried rows stay dried: reading dry macros against a drained wet weight is the bug this row closes. FDC has no canned-lentil food at all, so the macros are boiled lentils (172421) borrowed as the drained basis — the same coherence ruling the canned beans took — and the can weight is a typical label weight, not an FDC portion.

the plain-edamame row Frozen Edamame was standing in for — the same split as Peas. Linked to FDC 168411 (Edamame, frozen, prepared), the shelled cooked bean a recipe line means; Frozen Edamame keeps the unprepared frozen record and is unchanged

a tin of sweetcorn had nothing to land on: Corn is FDC 169998 (Corn, sweet, yellow, raw) with ear measures — fresh cobs. Linked to FDC 169214 (canned, whole kernel, drained solids), so the macros are the drained basis a can measure would multiply
the frozen bag beside the fresh cobs, FDC 168398 (frozen, kernels cut off cob, unprepared); Corn stays the fresh ear

the honest target a "cooked lentils" line was missing. It is NOT an alias of Canned Lentils — a pan of home-cooked lentils is not a drained tin — but both rest on the same FDC record: this row links 172421 directly, and Canned Lentils borrows it

Pasta, Spaghetti, Cavatappi and Ditalini all link FDC 169736 (Pasta, dry, enriched), so "2 cups cooked pasta" would have taken the dry basis — a ~2.3x kcal overcount. The dry rows keep their plain names, because a line that says "pasta" does mean the dry good
